response.query: What reproducibility standards (open code, synthetic/anonymized data, replication repository, restricted-data access protocols) will satisfy publishers, funders, and negotiators?
response.answer: To satisfy publishers, funders, and negotiators, adhere to open code, share anonymized data, use a replication repository, and follow restricted-data access protocols.

results.title: Reproducibility and Research Integrity - Parliament UK
results.content: Professor Timothy Bates at the University of Edinburgh suggested institutions could do this by supporting researchers who challenged popular claims, published studies which failed to replicate previous work, or whose work was independently replicated.108 Evidence from the UK Reproducibility Network Local Network Leads concurred. As Elsevier explained, in an effective research system, journals should employ peer review processes to interrogate authors’ use of methods, results and statistical analysis.201 The written evidence noted that the process failed to catch irreproducible work in some cases.202 Dr Jessica Butler, Analytical Lead and Research Fellow at the University of Aberdeen, explained how this process “actively disincentivised [early career researchers] from producing top-quality, reproducible research”:. UK Reproducibility Network Chair Professor Munafò built on the theme of registered reports—calling for a “registered reports partnership model” solution, where funding and the principles for a study were agreed concurrently, with a guarantee of publication.212 This model was expanded upon (drawing on Professor Munafò’s research) in written evidence submitted by nine university researchers, led by Dr Thomas Rhys Evans at the University of Greenwich.

results.title: A Pragmatic CDO's Field Guide to Data Quality — Part 10 ...
results.content: # **A Pragmatic CDO’s Field Guide to Data Quality — Part 10 — The CDO’s 12-Month Playbook: Operating Model, SLOs,** CoDQ**, and Change Management**. We define RACI at the CDE level, establish error budgets, incident response, and runbooks, and build a CoDQ (cost of poor data) model that rolls up to ROI. A maturity model with quarterly milestones guides progress. * **Capability Model Over Tools**: **Data quality (DQ)** initiatives succeed by focusing on core capabilities (**contracts**, **validation rules**, **observability**, **lineage**, **master data management (MDM)**, **reconciliation**, **privacy**, **ML quality**) rather than chasing shiny tools. This chapter presents a **DQ capability model** mapping each capability to concrete acceptance criteria, service-level objectives (SLOs), and evidence artifacts (like data quality scorecards and lineage…. ## Written by Adnan Masood, PhD. Dr. Adnan Masood is an Engineer, Thought Leader, Author, AI/ML PhD, Stanford Scholar, Harvard Alum, Microsoft Regional Director, and STEM Robotics Coach.
